source: Senate polling model, re-run Oct 25 on every public poll since Aug 1 in the 14 competitive races (247 polls through Oct 22: the ElectIndex poll feed plus hand-added releases; pollsters the feed bans are excluded, including Wedgewood Polls, which said on Oct 20 that its polls were fabricated): house effects estimated against other pollsters and shrunk, likely-voter adjustment, 14-day half-life. First run Oct 9; re-run Oct 21 and Oct 25.

notes.ID: Treated as safe R, as in the Oct 9 model. The two polls conflict: Advanced Targeting Research (Sept 16) had Achilles (I) ahead; Peak Insights (R-leaning, Sept 30) had Risch up 25.
notes.MT: Three-way race. Polls put Alme (R) at 44-45 with Bodnar (I) at 26-32 and Bankhead (D) at 14-24, so the margin shown is Alme vs. Bodnar.
notes.NE: Osborn is an independent. If he wins he counts for neither party here, as in the Oct 9 model.
notes.ME: Troy Jackson replaced Graham Platner as the Democratic nominee (special convention, July 25).
notes.SD: Bengs (I) is the main opponent; no Democrat on the ballot.

2026-10-21.note: Afternoon re-run without Wedgewood Polls (fabricated) and the feed-banned Big Data Poll and SoCal Strategies; the morning run had included them (NE was R+2.0, GA D+9.0, ME D+2.1, control 68%).
